nodes.title: In post-call analysis, a shadow-mode crisis-judge hit is recorded on the analysis (judge_shadow) and never written as a call_safety_event. Only a judge_raised hit becomes an RD3 'flagged' safety event.
nodes.rationale: Any call_safety_event row sets analysis.safety_violation (calls/analysis.ts). Learning reads safety_violation as an experiment guardrail (learning/index.ts, probe.ts tolerance 0), and the safety_event_rate monitor reads it too. A shadow hit written there would move experiments and monitors, so shadow would no longer change nothing, which breaks decision.2026-10-21.judge-raise-only-contract.
nodes.reverse_if: The owner sets mode 'raise' for post-call analysis, so hits are meant to count. Or safety_violation stops being derived from call_safety_event rows, and a separate shadow event type exists that no guardrail or monitor reads.

nodes.title: Showing a brain's first-token time under the label 'Reply gap'
nodes.tried: shared/stacks.ts gave the cascade stacks replyGap values such as '0.70 s first token'. The stack picker showed them under 'Reply gap', and the field is documented as the time from the caller finishing to her first audio.
nodes.broke: A first-token time leaves out end-of-turn detection, speech-to-text and the voice's first audio. So the picker overstated how fast she answers, for every cascade stack, and showed a person the jargon 'first token'.
nodes.instead: Each value names what was measured ('0.70 s, reply text starts'; '0.43 s, voice starts after the text'), and each source says the whole reply gap was not measured. A true end-to-end figure per stack waits for the deployed-host measurement. Fixed in d161603.
